newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSSIE RULES-Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules column.
newsitem.headline: AUSSIE RULES-Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
AFL SILLY SEASON COMES EARLY
Christmas is supposed to be the silly season for football but AFL premierships don't come much stranger than this one.
With two rounds remaining, 12 of the 16 teams have a chance of making the final eight.
While the chances of some are more realistic than others, it would be foolhardy to discount any team that is at least mathematically still in the race.
Best on Ground can hardly tip a winner, let alone say with any conviction which teams will and won't make it to the finals.

Only Geelong and St Kilda can lose both games from here and make the finals, while Adelaide, Sydney, West Coast and Western Bulldogs (third to sixth) could all finish as low as 10th if they were to drop their last two games.
Conversely -- or perversely, depending on which way you look at it -- any of the top seven teams can finish the season in first place.
How silly is that?
The top seven -- Geelong, St Kilda, Adelaide, Sydney, West Coast, Western Bulldogs and North Melbourne -- all have the form to be in the September action.
The eighth spot could go to any one of Brisbane, Port Adelaide, Fremantle, Collingwood or Carlton. The latter two were kept in the race by Saturday night's draw between the Lions and the Power.
If each of the first three win only one of their last two games, Brisbane will claim eighth by virtue of a superior points for-and-against percentage.
The Lions play Essendon at the Gabba this weekend but face West Coast in Perth the following week.

Port Adelaide have two matches which could go either way against Richmond at the MCG and St Kilda at Football Park, while Fremantle play Geelong in Perth and then Melbourne at the MCG in the final round.
Our tip? Port Adelaide to finish eighth and play Adelaide in the fourth qualifying final at Football Park.
IF YOU DON'T MIND, UMPIRE
Essendon can't make the finals but they could have snuffed out Collingwood's faint hopes had it not been for a fundamental umpiring error during Saturday's game at the MCG.
The Bombers trailed by 40 points at the final change but, when Matthew Lloyd kicked his third goal for the quarter, they crept to within 16 points and a stunning victory looked possible.
At the next centre bounce Magpie ruckman Damian Monkhorst had his number taken -- for the second time in the game -- for an incident involving Bomber small man Gary Moorcroft.
Surely if the umpire deemed the incident reportable he should also have considered it worthy of a 50-metre penalty, which would have taken Moorcroft to within goal-scoring range.
As it turned out, Moorcroft's free kick to the crowded half-forward line was swept away by the Collingwood defence and out of the danger zone.
The Pies held on to win by 10 points.
BUCKLEY REPORT A LOW POINT

Saturday's frenzied final quarter at the MCG threw Brownlow Medal markets into turmoil after second favorite Nathan Buckley was reported for allegedly kneeing Essendon's Barry Young in what is euphemistically referred to as "the groin area".
Before the report Buckley was the 7/2 second favourite behind St Kilda's Robert Harvey at 2/1. If Buckley is found guilty Harvey's odds will shorten to 11/8.
Some reports say Buckley will plead not guilty to the charge at the AFL tribunal tonight because Collingwood believe there is no video footage of the incident.
In that case, his fate could rest in Young's hands.
If the Bomber half-forward follows Trent Ormond-Allen's lead and confirms the incident took place, Buckley could be denied his medal chance.
Ormond-Allen told the tribunal that Carlton's Luke O'Sullivan broke his jaw in an off-the-ball incident at Football Park in round 18.
The incident was not captured on camera but O'Sullivan still copped four weeks.
*Andrew Bartram writes a regular AFL column for Reuters. Any feedback to michael.stapleton@reuters.com
